gap: No result ChatGPT got says that the 4-spool boxes these combos rely on handle damp filament in different ways. Creality's K2 Pro Combo CFS uses desiccant only ('Drying Method: Desiccant', no heater) and rejects TPU. Bambu's AMS 2 Pro on the P2S Combo heats to 65 °C, but its spec footnote says that is too cool to fully dry ABS, ASA, PET, PA, PC or the CF blends. The P2S itself has no heated chamber.
standout_why: Compared against the cited desktop3dprinters.us multicolor-enclosed list, which states chamber heat (P2S 'Passive, 50 °C', K2 Pro 'Active, 60 °C', Q2 'Active, 65 °C') but has no drying or materials column and never says what its chamber figure measures. Slot counts there use a different unit per maker: spools, units, colours, filaments or tools. ChatGPT's answer repeats 'actively heated chamber for engineering materials' for the K2 Pro and says nothing about whether any feeder dries filament. 3dprinterlist.com (the other cited page) failed on an SSL error and I could not read it. I did not open the other ten uncited results in this run, so I can't rule out that one of them states the drying split. The cited rival does not.
decides: This refines ChatGPT's ABS/ASA steer and doesn't overturn it. The K2 Pro Combo has the heated chamber (up to 60 °C) but its feeder can't dry, so hygroscopic engineering filament has to arrive dry or be dried in a separate dryer. The P2S Combo's box can dry, but at 65 °C, which Bambu's footnote (via 3DJake) calls too cool for ABS, ASA or nylon, and the printer has no chamber heat. For PLA/PETG multicolour, the P2S's heated-drying box is the real difference from the P1S. For ABS/ASA, a buyer of either should budget for a standalone dryer. QIDI Q2 ($449 at qidi3d.com today; Dealectric lists it) pairs a 65 °C active chamber with the QIDI Box ($228), but I could not open QIDI's page for the Box's drying spec, so it cannot be ranked on drying yet.
